issue: For the U.S.S.G. § 4B1.1 career offender enhancement, must a court decide whether a prior drug conviction is a controlled substance offense by the law in effect at the time of the prior conviction, or by the law in effect at the time of sentencing?

sides.position: Time-of-conviction: the prior offense is measured against the controlled-substance definition in effect when the defendant was convicted of it (per the dissent's grouping; the excerpts do not state which circuits adopt which rule, so this mapping is inferred and unconfirmed)

Time-of-sentencing: the prior offense is measured against the Guidelines and controlled-substance definition in effect at sentencing, as the Guidelines' directive in § 1B1.11 requires (per the majority's grouping; mapping inferred and unconfirmed)
cases: United States v. Minor, 121 F.4th 1085 (5th Cir. 2024)

this_court: time-of-sentencing (the majority adopts this rule and states the court 'has now picked a side' while awaiting Supreme Court resolution)
quote: As the majority points out, the circuits are deeply split over whether the correct approach to applying the § 4B1.1 enhancement is time-ofconviction or time-of-sentencing.
cite: United States v. Minor, 121 F.4th 1085 (5th Cir. 2024)
